---
title: Editor Setup
description: >
  Connect Panache to your editor, configure formatting on save, and enable
  semantic highlighting for Quarto and other Markdown flavors.
---

Set up Panache in your editor using the instructions below. Most integrations
start `panache lsp` automatically when you open a supported document. RStudio
uses the Panache R package's formatting addins instead.

For formatting, diagnostics, navigation, and code actions, see [Language
Server](language-server.qmd).

## Editor Configuration {#editor-configuration}

If you want to start the language server manually (for debugging), then you can
run `panache lsp` in your terminal. This will start the server and wait for
JSON-RPC input. But most users will want to set up their editor to start the
server automatically when editing supported files. See the editor integration
instructions below.

### Neovim

Install Panache through [Mason](https://github.com/mason-org/mason.nvim) with
`:MasonInstall panache`, or use one of the [CLI installation
methods](../getting-started.qmd#installation). The executable must be available
to Neovim on `PATH`.

With Neovim 0.11 or later and a current
[nvim-lspconfig](https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig) installed, enable its
built-in Panache configuration in your `init.lua`:

```lua
vim.lsp.enable("panache")
```

The configuration recognizes the `markdown`, `quarto`, and `rmd` filetypes and
starts `panache lsp`. Mason installs the binary; enabling the LSP configuration
connects it to your buffers.

Without nvim-lspconfig, define the configuration directly before enabling it:

```lua
vim.lsp.config("panache", {
  cmd = { "panache", "lsp" },
  filetypes = { "markdown", "quarto", "rmd" },
  root_markers = {
    ".panache.toml",
    "panache.toml",
    "_quarto.yml",
    "_bookdown.yml",
    ".git",
  },
})
vim.lsp.enable("panache")
```

For mdsvex files, register their filetype and add it to the server configuration
before enabling the server:

```lua
vim.filetype.add({
  extension = { svx = "mdsvex" },
  pattern = { [".*%.svelte%.md"] = "mdsvex" },
})
vim.lsp.config("panache", {
  filetypes = { "markdown", "quarto", "rmd", "mdsvex" },
})
```

To format on save:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufWritePre", {
  pattern = { "*.qmd", "*.md", "*.Rmd", "*.rmd", "*.svx", "*.svelte.md" },
  callback = function()
    vim.lsp.buf.format({ name = "panache", async = false })
  end,
})
```

Format the current buffer with `:lua vim.lsp.buf.format({ name = "panache" })`.

#### Conform

[conform.nvim](https://github.com/stevearc/conform.nvim) includes a Panache
formatter. With Panache installed on `PATH`, add it to your Conform setup:

```lua
require("conform").setup({
  formatters_by_ft = {
    markdown = { "panache" },
    quarto = { "panache" },
    rmd = { "panache" },
    mdsvex = { "panache" },
  },
  format_on_save = { timeout_ms = 3000 },
})
```

Conform sends the buffer and filename to Panache, so flavor detection and
project configuration apply. If you enable Conform's format-on-save option, omit
the LSP formatting autocmd above to avoid formatting twice. The language server
can still provide diagnostics and navigation.

### RStudio

The [Panache R package](https://github.com/jolars/panache-r) provides an
in-process formatter and RStudio addins. It is in early development. Install the
development version from GitHub; building from source requires Cargo and Rust
1.89 or newer:

```r
install.packages(c("remotes", "rstudioapi"))
remotes::install_github("jolars/panache-r")
```

Choose **Format with Panache** or **Format Selection with Panache** from
RStudio's **Addins** menu to format the active document or selected blocks. The
addins work on editor contents and discover `panache.toml` from the document's
directory. They leave the edits for you to save.

The package formats R code blocks through the Arity R package by default.
Explicitly configured external formatter commands must be installed on `PATH`.
It provides formatting; use the CLI or an LSP editor for Panache's lint checks.
See the [R package documentation](https://jolars.github.io/panache-r/) for
function arguments, configuration overrides, and addin options.

### VS Code

Install the [VS Code Marketplace
extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=jolars.panache).
The extension starts the language server automatically for supported files.

To install through the command line, run:

```bash
code --install-extension jolars.panache
```

If you prefer to install from the VS Code UI, launch VS Code Quick Open
(`Ctrl+P`), then run:

```sh
ext install jolars.panache
```

The extension launches `panache lsp` automatically.

Optional extension settings:

```json
{
  "panache.commandPath": "panache",
  "panache.downloadBinary": true,
  "panache.releaseTag": "latest",
  "panache.serverArgs": [],
  "panache.serverEnv": { "RUST_LOG": "info" },
  "panache.trace.server": "off"
}
```

### Open VSX (Positron, Cursor, VSCodium, etc.)

Install the [Open VSX extension](https://open-vsx.org/extension/jolars/panache).
The extension starts the language server automatically for supported files.

The Open VSX extension is identical to the VS Code extension and uses the same
configuration settings, so see the [VS Code] section above for configuration
instructions.

### Zed

Install the [Panache extension](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=panache) from
the extensions view (`zed: extensions` in the command palette). Markdown is
built into Zed, and Quarto comes from the [Quarto
extension](https://github.com/prefrontal-systems/zed-quarto-plugin), which you
need installed first. Zed has no R Markdown language extension, so Panache's R
Markdown support is unavailable there for now.

Zed uses the `panache` on your `PATH` when there is one, and otherwise downloads
the release binary matching your platform. Keeping Panache on the `PATH` is the
better option on distributions that cannot run the generic release build, NixOS
above all.

To format on save, add to `settings.json`:

```json
{
  "languages": {
    "Markdown": {
      "formatter": "language_server",
      "format_on_save": "on"
    }
  }
}
```

Formatting and linting options come from `panache.toml` (see
[Configuration](../reference/configuration.qmd)). Zed's `lsp` settings block
cannot supply them: the server reads its configuration from disk and accepts no
formatting settings over LSP.

To point Zed at a particular binary, set `binary.path`:

```json
{
  "lsp": {
    "panache-language-server": {
      "binary": { "path": "/opt/panache/bin/panache", "arguments": ["lsp"] }
    }
  }
}
```

### Helix

Add to `~/.config/helix/languages.toml`:

```toml
[[language]]
name = "markdown"
language-servers = ["panache"]
auto-format = true

[[language]]
name = "quarto"
language-servers = ["panache"]
auto-format = true

[[language]]
name = "rmarkdown"
language-servers = ["panache"]
auto-format = true

[language-server.panache]
command = "panache"
args = ["lsp"]
```

Format the current file with `:format` or `<space>f`.

### Emacs

Using `lsp-mode`:

```elisp
(require 'lsp-mode)

;; Define panache LSP client
(lsp-register-client
 (make-lsp-client
  :new-connection (lsp-stdio-connection '("panache" "lsp"))
  :activation-fn (lsp-activate-on "quarto" "markdown" "rmarkdown")
  :server-id 'panache))

;; Enable for specific modes
(add-hook 'markdown-mode-hook #'lsp-deferred)
(add-hook 'quarto-mode-hook #'lsp-deferred)

;; Format on save
(add-hook 'before-save-hook #'lsp-format-buffer nil t)
```

### Sublime Text

Using LSP package:

1. Install [LSP](https://packagecontrol.io/packages/LSP) package
2. Add to LSP settings:

```json
{
  "clients": {
    "panache": {
      "enabled": true,
      "command": ["panache", "lsp"],
      "selector": "text.html.markdown | source.quarto"
    }
  }
}
```

### Kate

Kate supports LSP servers via its LSP client plugin:

1. Enable the LSP Client plugin
2. Add to LSP client configuration:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "markdown": {
      "command": ["panache", "lsp"],
      "highlightingModeRegex": "^Markdown$"
    }
  }
}
```

## Project Configuration

Put formatting and linting settings in `panache.toml`. The language server reads
these settings from disk, so they apply across editors and the CLI. See
[Configuration](configure.qmd) for project setup and [Configuration
Discovery](language-server.qmd#configuration-discovery) for precedence and
reload behavior.

To use a custom user config in VS Code, set the environment variable in your
user `settings.json`:

```json
{
  "panache.serverEnv": {
    "PANACHE_CONFIG": "P:/Softwares/panache.toml"
  }
}
```

Run **Panache: Restart Server** after changing `panache.serverEnv`. Project
configs take precedence over this fallback. A missing or invalid
`PANACHE_CONFIG` file is reported as a configuration error, and formatting is
refused until it is fixed.

## Semantic Tokens

Panache uses custom semantic-token types for Pandoc and Quarto syntax. Map these
types to colors in your editor to enable the additional highlighting. See
[Semantic Tokens](language-server.qmd#semantic-tokens) for the supported syntax
and flavor behavior.

In VS Code (`settings.json`):

```json
"editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations": {
  "enabled": true,
  "rules": {
    "citation": "#c586c0",
    "crossref": "#4ec9b0",
    "shortcode": "#dcdcaa",
    "div": "#569cd6",
    "math": "#ce9178",
    "footnote": "#9cdcfe",
    "attribute": "#b5cea8"
  }
}
```

In Neovim, link the LSP semantic-token groups to your colorscheme:

```lua
for token, group in pairs({
  citation = "@markup.link",
  crossref = "@markup.link.label",
  shortcode = "@function.macro",
  div = "@keyword.directive",
  math = "@markup.math",
  footnote = "@markup.link.label",
  attribute = "@attribute",
}) do
  vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, "@lsp.type." .. token, { link = group })
end
```

## Troubleshooting

### LSP Not Starting

Check that panache is in your PATH:

```bash
which panache
```

Test the LSP manually:

```bash
panache lsp
# Should start and wait for JSON-RPC input
```

### Formatting Not Working

Enable LSP logging in your editor to see error messages:

#### Neovim

```lua
vim.lsp.set_log_level("debug")
-- View logs: :lua vim.cmd('e'..vim.lsp.get_log_path())
```

#### VS Code

Set `"panache.trace.server": "verbose"` in settings.

### Configuration Not Loading

Verify your config file is valid by testing with the CLI first:

```bash
panache format --config .panache.toml test.qmd
```

Configuration discovery starts from the document's directory. See [Configuration
Discovery](language-server.qmd#configuration-discovery) for precedence and
reload behavior.
